data.title: AES GAAP EPS of $0.76, revenue of $3.87B beats by $700M
Telus targets $900M annualized cash savings exiting 2028 while projecting $500M AI infrastructure revenue over 3 years
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: TELUS (T:CA) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "Our transformation strategy has one clear objective, and that is to solidify TELUS' position as the leading communications and AI infrastructure player in Canada" (CEO, President & Director Victor Dodig). Dodig described "an intentional and a strategic pivot to profitable growth" built around strengthening the balance sheet, tightening operating discipline, and reallocating resources toward the core telecom business and AI infrastructure.
  • "We're committed to strengthening our balance sheet and have a clear path to achieving a net debt to adjusted EBITDA leverage ratio of 3x or lower by the end of 2028" (CEO, President & Director Dodig). He reiterated actions previously announced in Q2: "We reset our dividend payout ratio... terminated the dilutive discount on the dividend investment -- reinvestment plan, and we put a moratorium on acquisitions," while emphasizing a focus on "monetization strategy for our noncore assets" and "unlock equity value from our PureFibre network while maintaining control."
  • "Today, we are announcing a program that targets $900 million in annualized cash savings exiting 2028" (CEO, President & Director Dodig). He added that "Up to 80% of these run rate savings are expected to come from telecom," and cited additional consumer pivots, including moving "home security" and "TV offerings to a capital-light model" and "winding down unprofitable and capital-intensive initiatives," with "approximately $250 million in structural cash savings" expected to fully run-rate "beginning in 2027."
  • "Basic EPS was negative $0.42 due to the TELUS Health noncash impairment" (Chief Financial Officer Gopi Chande). Chande also reported "Consolidated service revenue of $4.5 billion" and "Consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $1.8 billion," plus "free cash flow of $396 million" and leverage of "3.6x" as of September 30.

Outlook

  • "For the full year 2026, we are reaffirming our consolidated guidance as updated with our Q2 results in July" (CFO Chande). He restated: "service revenue of flat to negative 2%, adjusted EBITDA of negative 2% to negative 4%, capital expenditures of approximately $2.6 billion and free cash flow of approximately $1.8 billion."
  • "We have a pipeline today of more than $1 billion in total contract value across our digital infrastructure business" (CEO, President & Director Dodig). Dodig added, "over the next 3 years, we project about $500 million in revenue with healthy margins," and management clarified in Q&A that "$500 million" is "a cumulative number" (EVP and President of Business Solutions, Health, Agriculture, Consumer Goods & Partner Solutions Navin Arora).
  • Compared with Q2, management did not introduce a new full-year 2026 range, maintaining the July update; the Q3 call added a detailed multi-year efficiency target and more explicit AI infrastructure revenue framing.

Financial Results

  • "Consolidated service revenue of $4.5 billion was lower by 1% year-over-year" (CFO Chande), while "Consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $1.8 billion declined by 5%," which he said was "primarily due to weaker results in TELUS Digital" and the prior-year impact of "$78 million of onetime items."
  • "Mobile phone net additions of 84,000" and "blended mobile phone churn landing at 1.01% for the quarter" were highlighted as key operating metrics, alongside "postpaid churn" that "improved to below 0.9%" (CFO Chande). He also said "Mobile network revenue of $1.8 billion was up 1%" and "Fixed data revenue of $1.2 billion increased by 2%."
  • "We recorded a noncash goodwill impairment of $800 million for our TELUS Health business" (CFO Chande). He attributed it to "updated growth expectations, broader market conditions and current valuation perspectives from ongoing strategic processes," while stating, "it does not change our commitment to TELUS Health."
  • "In order to achieve the $900 million target, we expect to invest approximately $150 million" (CFO Chande), and he reported liquidity of "$3 billion" and a quarterly dividend of "$0.1875 per share."

Q&A

  • Maher Yaghi, Scotiabank: asked about "the revenue opportunity for TELUS" and "where... growth could come from"; CEO Dodig said the plan combines "$900 million" cash savings, "monetize our noncore assets," and "unlock some of the equity value" in PureFibre, while EVP David Fuller added, "we can continue to grow the telecom business in the low single digits... both top and bottom line going forward."
  • Drew McReynolds, RBC: probed the composition of "$900 million"; CFO Chande said the split is "roughly 50-50 CapEx and EBITDA," defined as "$75 million in December 2028 times 12," with "$150 million" of upfront investment; Drew also asked about the "$500 million" AI revenue number, and Arora replied, "That is a cumulative number."
  • Stephanie Price, CIBC: asked about PureFibre equitization and "retaining control"; CFO Chande said the aim is to "surface the significant value" to "strengthen our balance sheet," while Fuller stated, "we are going to absolutely maintain control" and "it is not... focused on the wholesale side of the business."
  • Vince Valentini, TD Cowen: pressed on wireless quality and Public Mobile; Fuller responded, "Q3 was actually a very restrained approach to promotional intensity," adding, "our success on net adds was entirely driven by our success in churn" and "it was not driven by Public loading at all."
  • Tim Casey, BMO: asked to reconcile a prior "$2 billion" AI narrative versus current "$500 million"; CEO Dodig said the company made "a refinement to our strategic narrative," and Arora said the earlier framing "included a lot of the TELUS digital elements" that have been removed from the current infrastructure-focused pillars.
  • David McFadgen, ATB Cormark: asked what TELUS Health is "worth now" post-impairment and about eliminating the DRIP; CFO Chande said, "I'm not going to comment on the specific valuation of TELUS Health," and on the DRIP, "it's not something that's on our radar right now" due to "low uptake."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Slightly negative analyst tone centered on proof of savings, valuation, and AI sizing, including questions like "How do we square that" and requests for valuation "ballpark" (Tim Casey, BMO; David McFadgen, ATB Cormark).
  • Slightly positive management tone emphasized execution confidence, including "We know how to do this, and we're going to get it done" (CEO, President & Director Dodig) and "we're confident in its delivery" (CFO Chande), while avoiding valuation specifics ("stay away from anchoring on any valuation," CFO Chande).
  • Versus Q2, Q3 carried a more concrete, quantified operational-efficiency posture (explicit $900M target) and more pointed analyst scrutiny on reconciling AI opportunity sizing and impairment implications.

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Q3 introduced a new quantified efficiency program: "targets $900 million in annualized cash savings exiting 2028" (CEO, President & Director Dodig), whereas in Q2 Dodig said, "I expect to provide a detailed overview... on or before our third quarter earnings call in November" (CEO, President & Director Dodig).
  • Q3 added a specific AI infrastructure revenue framing: "we project about $500 million in revenue" over 3 years (CEO, President & Director Dodig), while Q2 focused on building "sustainable sovereign AI data centers" without giving a comparable multi-year revenue projection in prepared remarks (CEO, President & Director Dodig).
  • Impairments shifted from TELUS Digital in Q2 ("pretax noncash carrying value impairment of $2.1 billion," CFO Chande) to TELUS Health in Q3 ("noncash goodwill impairment of $800 million," CFO Chande), with both calls tying impairments to changing expectations and market conditions.

Risks and Concerns

  • "Service revenue... was lower by 1%" and EBITDA pressure were linked to "weaker results in TELUS Digital" and "hyperscale client volume ramp-downs" (CFO Chande), with management framing mitigation as tighter pricing/terms, automation, and overhead reduction (CEO, President & Director Dodig).
  • Management cited execution and timing risk around monetization and fiber equitization, stressing control and process discipline: "We'll manage these engagements on our terms" (CEO, President & Director Dodig) and "we're still defining our perimeter" (CFO Chande).
  • On AI infrastructure, management emphasized disciplined pacing: "use the assets we have first, then add GPU capacity as customer demand materializes" (CEO, President & Director Dodig) and "we're not going to boil the ocean" (EVP Arora).

Final Takeaway

TELUS management framed Q3 as a shift from outlining a transformation to quantifying it, anchored by a $900 million annualized cash-savings program exiting 2028, continued deleveraging toward 3x net debt to adjusted EBITDA by 2028, and a Canadian-focused AI infrastructure plan that includes a pipeline of more than $1 billion in total contract value and a projected $500 million of cumulative revenue over the next 3 years. Management paired these targets with reaffirmed 2026 guidance ranges from Q2, while acknowledging pressure in TELUS Digital and recording an $800 million noncash TELUS Health goodwill impairment tied to updated expectations and market conditions.

data.title: Haypp outlines 18%-25% CAGR to 2028 and 5.5% adjusted EBIT margin target while rebalancing U.S./U.K. marketing
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Haypp Group AB (HYGRF) Q3 2026

Management view

  • "This quarter saw each of our segments perform in line with their roles. Core markets delivered 61% EBITDA growth, funding our operations in growth markets, which in turn grew 54% in revenue." (President & CEO Gavin O'Dowd)
  • "We're happy to see continued robust growth in nicotine pouches to 33% year-on-year despite tougher comparators in the U.S." (President & CEO O'Dowd)
  • "Gross margins were up to a record high... We have increased the investment in marketing expenditure to accelerate our new customer inflow while the window remains open. This led to a reduction in EBIT margins, which we expect to continue for the remainder of this year before trending back towards our 2028 guidance." (President & CEO O'Dowd)
  • "Net sales reached SEK 1.221 billion, an increase of 28.2% as reported and 25.7% at constant currency." (Chief Financial Officer Peter Deli)
  • "Adjusted EBIT was SEK 26.3 million... The margin compression, therefore, reflects deliberate investment in G&A capabilities and marketing, not a problem in gross profit generation." (Chief Financial Officer Deli)
  • "Haypp announced a financial provision to allow for settlement of an alleged violation of local regulations in the U.S. city... The group has established a $2.5 million provision." (President & CEO O'Dowd)

Outlook

  • "This led to a reduction in EBIT margins, which we expect to continue for the remainder of this year before trending back towards our 2028 guidance." (President & CEO O'Dowd)
  • "Revenue growth of 18% to 25% CAGR from 2024 at a constant currency and a 5.5% adjusted EBIT margin, plus or minus 150 basis points, subject to the investment opportunities, which remain at the time." (President & CEO O'Dowd)
  • "For the coming quarters, the focus is execution and discipline, reduce and reallocate marketing investment, preserve the initiatives that work." (Chief Financial Officer Deli)
  • "From an outside perspective, I think I would view this one as the overall profitability within the U.S. is not expected to change materially." (President & CEO O'Dowd)

Financial results

  • "Gross profit increased by 34.8% to SEK 241 million... gross margin increased by 1 percentage point to a new all-time high of 19.7%." (Chief Financial Officer Peter Deli)
  • "The increase in gross profit was mainly driven by Media & Insights increasing to 12.2% of group net sales, up 1.1 percentage points year-on-year." (Chief Financial Officer Deli)
  • "Adjusted overheads were SEK 185.5 million or 15.2% of net sales... The biggest driver for the overhead change versus Q2 2026 is clearly the marketing investment. It increased to 3.2% of net sales from 1% last year." (Chief Financial Officer Deli)
  • "Inventory decreased sequentially to SEK 315 million from SEK 368 million... Net debt decreased sequentially to SEK 96.3 million from SEK 222 million... Cash and cash equivalents were SEK 174 million at quarter end." (Chief Financial Officer Deli)

Q&A

  • "On the marketing cut or reallocation rather in Q4... could you give us a sense of how sort of significant that reduction will be in Q4?" (Morayo Adesina, Barclays Bank PLC) "What we will do is continue to balance the shape of where that investment is coming between how much of it is going directly towards generating awareness... versus how much is around the consumer offer." (President & CEO O'Dowd)
  • "Could you give us any more details on what the alleged violations relate to... and also which city it involves?" (Kristian Bergström-Smolle, Pareto Securities) "No, I can't, to be frank... There is a confidentiality restriction on this one." (President & CEO O'Dowd)
  • "What are you basing that assumption on?" (Bergström-Smolle, Pareto Securities) "We are in robust -- we're in solid engagement... so we're feeling reasonably confident with the statement that we've made already." (President & CEO O'Dowd)
  • "Just wondering which channels or activities you are planning on dropping maybe." (Bergström-Smolle, Pareto Securities) "Particularly on the lower funnel marketing... many of those new customers... it would have come to us organically anyway... So hence, we feel as though we're happy to trim that back." (President & CEO O'Dowd)
  • "Are you seeing greater engagement? And how much further runway is there to broaden the number or scope of these offerings?" (Daniel Tharian, Deutsche Bank) "We do the development during the year... we do the live testing in Q4 and then we roll out in Q1." (President & CEO O'Dowd)
  • "Could you just give a sense of the scale of that today?" (Tharian, Deutsche Bank) "Subscriptions, in particular, is showing an excellent exponential growth... we consider our subscriptions to be a really valid offer at this point in time." (President & CEO O'Dowd)
  • "Is Haypp doing any preparation for this in development?" (Written question on AI) "Absolutely, we are... we definitely envisage that the future of search is going to move... into large language models... we have been doing a huge amount of work in this over the past 3 years." (President & CEO O'Dowd)
  • "We launched in Saudi Arabia in the beginning of the quarter... sales start off quite slowly, but they are growing exponentially... we don't expect it to be a notable part of the business imminently." (President & CEO O'Dowd)

Sentiment analysis

  • "Just wondering here because you say it will have no direct impact on your future sales in the U.S. What are you basing that assumption on?" (Kristian Bergström-Smolle, Pareto Securities) and "Could you give us any more details... and also which city it involves?" (Bergström-Smolle, Pareto Securities) reflected a slightly negative/skeptical tone centered on the U.S. provision and underlying assumptions.
  • "The margin compression... reflects deliberate investment..." (Chief Financial Officer Peter Deli) and "we're feeling reasonably confident" (President & CEO Gavin O'Dowd) reflected a slightly positive, controlled tone, while maintaining confidentiality: "No, I can't, to be frank." (President & CEO O'Dowd)
  • "This quarter saw each of our segments perform in line with their roles" (President & CEO O'Dowd) aligned with Q2’s confidence framing: "Our fundamentals remain solid and exactly as planned." (Chief Financial Officer Deli, Q2 2026)

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Q3 shifted emphasis from Q2’s acceleration language—"fastest volume and sales year-on-year growth since we IPO-ed" (President & CEO Gavin O'Dowd, Q2 2026)—to sustaining investment while optimizing: "reduce and reallocate marketing investment" (Chief Financial Officer Peter Deli, Q3 2026) and "we are reducing the spending on this area in Q4" (President & CEO O'Dowd, Q3 2026).
  • Q3 introduced a new disclosed item versus Q2: "The group has established a $2.5 million provision." (President & CEO O'Dowd, Q3 2026), while Q2’s U.S. discussion focused on "the FDA announced a level of enforcement discretion" (President & CEO O'Dowd, Q2 2026).
  • Q3 updated U.S. assortment commentary with explicit SKU action—"Haypp launching 68 new SKUs during the quarter" (President & CEO O'Dowd, Q3 2026)—versus Q2’s forward view that "the SKU count could double over the next year or so" (Daniel Tharian, Deutsche Bank: Question; President & CEO O'Dowd: Answer context, Q2 2026).

Risks and concerns

  • "Haypp announced a financial provision to allow for settlement of an alleged violation of local regulations in the U.S. city" and "There is a confidentiality restriction on this one." (President & CEO Gavin O'Dowd)
  • "The most relevant piece of legislation for Haypp will relate to marketing restrictions and is expected to come into place at the beginning of June 2027." (President & CEO O'Dowd)
  • "As you see more pouches sitting within a can, you will undoubtedly see a lower increase in the number of cans that goes through." (President & CEO O'Dowd)

Final takeaway

Management characterized Q3 as a quarter where core profitability funded growth-market expansion, while deliberate marketing and capability investments continued to pressure near-term EBIT margin. Executives reiterated the 2028 targets (18% to 25% revenue CAGR from 2024 at constant currency and a 5.5% adjusted EBIT margin ±150 basis points), described plans to reduce and reallocate marketing spend, and highlighted category and platform developments in the U.S. (expanded regulatory momentum and 68 new SKUs launched). Management also disclosed a $2.5 million provision tied to an alleged local-regulation violation in a U.S. city, while stating it expects no material operational or sales impact and emphasizing ongoing settlement discussions under confidentiality constraints.

data.title: Baytex targets 76,000-79,000 BOE/d in 2027 while outlining 8%-10% annual growth through 2029
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Baytex Energy Corp. (BTE) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "We continue to execute our strategy with strong performance across our portfolio, unlocking an opportunity-rich set of growth options, driving long-term value for shareholders." (President, CEO & Director Chad Lundberg). Management tied the “accelerated growth plan” to “improved capital efficiency, lower costs and execution across the Duvernay and heavy oil portfolio,” adding, "This acceleration is driven by efficiency gains, not a change in our commitment to capital discipline." (President, CEO & Director Lundberg)
  • Lundberg highlighted Q3 operating and capital return markers, including production averaging 71,600 BOE/d, record Duvernay production of 12,800 BOE/d, $139M of free cash flow, $165M returned via buybacks and the base dividend, and exiting with net cash of $522M.
  • Arthur detailed Duvernay and heavy oil execution and inventory changes, including 30-day IP rates of 1,489 BOE/d per well on a 5-well Duvernay pad and drilling/completion costs of $930 per foot. "Tuck-in acquisitions completed during the year increased our Duvernay land position by 16% to 106,000 net acres." (Chief Operating Officer Kendall Arthur)
  • "We generated adjusted funds flow of $332 million, or $0.48 per basic share." (Executive VP & CFO Chad Kalmakoff). He said 2026 exploration and development expenditures are now expected to be $665M, and cited guidance changes to royalty rate, operating costs, and transportation costs.

Outlook

  • Management issued 2027 guidance: "For 2027, we expect production of 76,000 BOE to 79,000 BOE per day, representing 7% to 11% annual growth with exploration and development expenditures of $775 million to $850 million." (President, CEO & Director Lundberg)
  • Lundberg framed 2027 as a step-change year: "This is the first year of full Duvernay commercialization, which drives Q4 to Q4 growth of 15%." He added, "This program achieves a sustaining capital breakeven of $50 per barrel in 2027, down from $52 in 2026." (President, CEO & Director Lundberg)
  • Kalmakoff described shareholder returns and capital flexibility for 2027: "For 2027, we have initially allocated $150 million to share repurchases under the normal course issuer bid with flexibility to adjust depending on market conditions. We expect to maintain the quarterly dividend at $0.0225 per share." (Executive VP & CFO Kalmakoff)
  • Compared with Q2, the company’s growth framework shifted from "grow production 6% to 8% annually" (President, CEO & Director Lundberg, Q2) to a stated "target 8% to 10% annual production growth" in the updated 3-year outlook (President, CEO & Director Lundberg, Q3), alongside a higher 2026 spending expectation.

Financial Results

  • Kalmakoff reported Q3 adjusted funds flow of $332M ($0.48/basic share) and free cash flow of $139M ($0.20/basic share), after exploration and development expenditures of $186M.
  • Shareholder returns in Q3 were described as $165M total, including 24M shares repurchased for $149M and a quarterly dividend of $0.0225/share, alongside a period-end net cash position of $522M.
  • Management updated select 2026 cost and other guidance items: royalty rate guidance to approximately 16%, operating costs expected to be approximately $13.30/BOE, and transportation costs expected to be approximately $3.75/BOE. (Executive VP & CFO Kalmakoff)

Q&A

  • Menno Hulshof, TD Cowen: Asked what Baytex needs to see to scale Peavine waterflood and how it could fit into the 3-year plan; President, CEO & Director Lundberg said key measures include injectability, "GOR suppression," and "offsetting production response through decline," adding, "I think we expect to see it by mid-2027" and that additional capital could be "in the $20 million to $30 million range" starting mid-2027.
  • Menno Hulshof, TD Cowen: Asked about Duvernay land competition and whether Viking could be monetized; President, CEO & Director Lundberg said, "it's very competitive" and described the strategy as pursuing "sections, not townships" going forward, while adding on Viking, "It's not core to the business... at the right time, we would look to try to potentially monetize the asset," tied to acting "contracyclically."
  • Greg Pardy, RBC: Pressed on whether there is "another Gemini" in the legacy land base; President, CEO & Director Lundberg referenced 750,000 acres, "1,100... risked locations" and "2,300 unrisked locations," and later added, "there are things we're working on today beyond modular SAGD... that we're just not talking about" due to readiness and competitive sensitivity; Pardy responded, "I don't think you want to answer my question."
  • Greg Pardy, RBC: Asked Duvernay product mix at 25,000 BOE/d and whether inflation is embedded; President, CEO & Director Lundberg gave a rule-of-thumb for new wells ("65% oil, 25% liquids, 10% gas") and later-life mix ("40% oil, 40% liquids, 20% gas"), said 2028 would model "right in the middle," and added, "we have built... lower single digits" inflation into the plan.
  • Amir Arif, ATB Cormark: Questioned drivers of operating cost improvement amid inflation; President, CEO & Director Lundberg cited higher volumes spreading fixed costs and described operational changes (proactive maintenance and timers on lower producers) that he said were flowing through repair and maintenance.
  • Amir Arif, ATB Cormark: Asked about decline rate trajectory and Gemini inclusion; President, CEO & Director Lundberg said the corporate decline "doesn't go up, it ticks down moderately through the plan" even "without the Clearwater waterflood success," and said Gemini has "$10 million in the plan today," with an additional "$50 million roughly" potentially added in late 2027 if FID occurs, with "first oil in 2029."
  • George Burwell, Jefferies: Asked about flexibility for Gemini under lower prices/wider differentials and asked for the bucketed increase to the $800M 2027 plan; President, CEO & Director Lundberg said stress tests still showed capacity with a "fortified balance sheet," and then broke the build to $800M into incremental Duvernay capital, incremental heavy oil activity, EOR, and Gemini delineation spending.
  • Webcast Q&A: Asked about 2027 shareholder returns and hedging; Executive VP & CFO Kalmakoff said the dividend plan remains "$0.09 per year" and buybacks are "initial $150 million" with flexibility, and added, "Nothing on for 2027 at this point" for WCS hedges and "not looking to put on any WTI hedges."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analyst sentiment was slightly negative to neutral at points, with sharper skepticism when RBC pressed for specifics: "I don't think you want to answer my question." (Greg Pardy, RBC). Other questions were oriented toward execution details and downside planning (waterflood scale-up gates, Gemini flexibility, cost drivers).
  • Management sentiment in prepared remarks was positive and confident, repeatedly emphasizing acceleration: "What has changed is the pace." (President, CEO & Director Lundberg). In Q&A, tone shifted to more guarded on undisclosed opportunities ("we're just not talking about") while remaining assertive on balance sheet capacity ("rock-solid, ironclad balance sheet").
  • Versus Q2, management language leaned more toward acceleration and commercialization milestones (full Duvernay commercialization in 2027; Duvernay 25,000 BOE/d timing pulled forward), while Q2 emphasized raised full-year production guidance with capital held flat and included board changes and an investor-relations retirement acknowledgment.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Guidance and strategy language shifted from Q2’s raised 2026 production guidance with "no change to our capital program of $625 million" (President, CEO & Director Lundberg, Q2) to Q3’s increase in expected 2026 exploration and development expenditures to $665M (Executive VP & CFO Kalmakoff, Q3) and a higher-growth 2027–2029 framing.
  • The Duvernay timeline was pulled forward: Q3 stated Baytex expects Duvernay to reach 25,000 BOE/d "in the second half of 2028, 1.5 years earlier than our previous plan" (President, CEO & Director Lundberg), whereas Q2 positioned 2027 as the year to "run a full commercial program." (President, CEO & Director Lundberg, Q2)
  • Analyst focus rotated from Q2’s questions on buyback pacing/SIB and early Duvernay completion learnings to Q3’s deeper interrogation of Gemini capital flexibility, waterflood scaling criteria, and the composition of incremental 2027 capex.

Risks and Concerns

  • Management flagged macro uncertainty: "we're in a bit of a choppy environment with respect to macro right now" (President, CEO & Director Lundberg), while asserting the net cash position provides flexibility for buybacks and potential Gemini spend.
  • Inflation and cost pressures were addressed as a planning assumption: "we have built... lower single digits into the plan" for items including "steel" and "diesel fuel" (President, CEO & Director Lundberg), with reliance on continued efficiency gains as the offset.
  • Waterflood and Gemini remain gating items with timing and commercialization risk; management repeatedly pointed to required technical signals (waterflood) and external inputs such as the "royalty framework" and utility requirements (Gemini). (President, CEO & Director Lundberg)

Final Takeaway

Baytex management positioned Q3 as a pivot toward faster growth driven by operating efficiency: 2027 production guidance of 76,000–79,000 BOE/d, a 3-year target of 8%–10% annual growth, and an accelerated Duvernay ramp to 25,000 BOE/d in H2 2028. Executives emphasized balance sheet capacity (net cash exiting Q3) to support increased spending, continued buybacks and the base dividend, while keeping flexibility around waterflood scale-up and a potential Gemini FID in H2 2027 with first oil targeted in 2029.

data.title: Berkshire Hathaway utility asks California regulators for 57% rate increase
data.description:
Berkshire Hathaway's (BRK.B) (BRK.A) Pacific Power utility asked California regulators Friday to approve a 57% rate increase that would hike the typical residential electricity bill by $120/month.

The increase would boost the utility's base revenue by $103M/year and reflects capital spending already under way to safeguard the grid.

Pacific Power's equipment has allegedly been tied to two blazes in California: the 2020 Slater Fire that burned more than 150K and killed two people and the 2022 McKinney Fire that burned 60K acres and killed four people.

Utility President Ryan Flynn told The Wall Street Journal that the company is swapping wooden power poles for steel and fiberglass structures and replacing hundreds of miles of bare wire with insulated, fire-resistant conductor.

Beyond the rate case, Pacific Power faces $637M in liability claims and legal expenses stemming from the 2020 and 2022 fires, and it is asking regulators to let it recover $340.5M of that sum from customers.

Pacific Power's Northern California territory sweeps across 11,292 square miles from the coast to the Nevada border, serving ~46K customers—about four customers per square mile; the utility also operates in Oregon, where it has ~630K customers.

data.title: Saputo expects $1.7B UK dairy division sale to close in H2 FY27 as it creates dedicated Ingredients Division
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Saputo Inc. (SAP:CA) Q2 fiscal 2027

Management View

  • Saputo reported what CEO Carl Colizza described as a “strong second quarter,” highlighting “14% growth in adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations and margin expansion to over 10%,” while saying “high protein ingredients remain the primary driver of adjusted EBITDA growth and margin expansion in the quarter” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Carl Colizza).
  • Management emphasized portfolio simplification and organizational changes, including the sale of the Dairy Division (UK) and the creation of a standalone ingredients unit. Colizza said, “we've created a dedicated Ingredients Division led by Steve Douglas to sharpen our commercial focus, accelerate innovation and expand our opportunities in global markets,” and added that “these organizational changes do not alter our strategic priorities” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).
  • Colizza also described operational focus and category investments, saying U.S. “network optimization, warehouse consolidation and manufacturing efficiencies are delivering productivity gains and lower costs,” and that demand is “running ahead of our capacity in categories like cottage cheese and string cheese,” prompting investments including “New string capacity at Las Cruces” and “our cottage cheese expansion at Friendship” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).
  • CFO Maxime Therrien framed Q2 around earnings growth, cash generation, and capital returns: “Adjusted EBITDA increased approximately 14% or $53 million to $438 million,” “Revenues were $4.3 billion, up approximately 4% in Q2,” and “we intend to file with the Toronto Stock Exchange to renew our NCIB which expires on November 18, 2026” (CFO & Secretary Maxime Therrien).
  • Colizza flagged leadership changes and enterprise transformation work, stating, “Haig Poutchigian, as Chief Enterprise Transformation Officer, is bringing our enterprise services together to accelerate technology adoption, improve productivity and speed up execution,” and “Dave Paradis now leads our Canadian division with a clear mandate: strengthen commercial execution, deepen our customer partnerships and drive operational excellence” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).

Outlook

  • Saputo did not provide formal EPS or revenue guidance in the prepared remarks or Q&A in this transcript; management instead emphasized structural demand drivers and continued investment in capacity and productivity.
  • Management reiterated fiscal 2027 capital plans from continuing operations, with Therrien saying, “For fiscal '27, we continue to expect approximately $500 million in CapEx from continuing operations, which now excludes the U.K.” (CFO & Secretary Therrien).
  • On portfolio-related forward items, Therrien said the Dairy Division (UK) sale “is expected to close in the second half of fiscal '27 for estimated proceeds of approximately CAD 1.7 billion,” and that Saputo “continue[s] to expect the sale of our interest in the Danone Saputo Dairy Australia joint venture to close in the third quarter of fiscal '27,” with proceeds “estimated to be approximately $250 million” (CFO & Secretary Therrien).
  • On ingredient pricing and sustainability, Colizza told analysts the company is not underwriting peak conditions: “none of our assumptions, either in CapEx returns or in our confidence as we move forward is built on those peak returns” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).

Financial Results

  • Saputo reported Q2 revenues of $4.3 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $438 million with a 10.3% margin (CFO & Secretary Therrien).
  • Net earnings from continuing operations were $213 million (or $0.53 per share), while “adjusted EPS increased 28% to $0.55,” which Therrien said reflected “stronger earnings and the impact of our share repurchases” (CFO & Secretary Therrien).
  • Cash flow and capital deployment were central themes: “Net cash from operating activities from continued operation was strong at $374 million,” Q2 capital expenditures were $78 million, and the company “returned approximately $300 million to shareholders in the quarter” via buybacks and dividends (CFO & Secretary Therrien).
  • By sector, Therrien reported Canada adjusted EBITDA of $179 million (12.7% margin), U.S. adjusted EBITDA of $205 million (9.6% margin), and international (Australia) adjusted EBITDA of $54 million (7.7% margin) (CFO & Secretary Therrien).
  • Leverage commentary included both reported and pro forma framing: “Our net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio ended the quarter at 1.55x,” and “by including the estimated net proceeds of the U.K. transaction, that ratio would be ... 0.52x,” while reiterating, “Our long-term target remains 2.25x” (CFO & Secretary Therrien).

Q&A

  • Irene Nattel, RBC Capital Markets: asked whether performance was overly dependent on ingredients; President Colizza said demand extends across “cottage cheese,” “yogurt,” “a variety of value-added and fortified beverages,” and added on ingredients, “we have experienced ... a real peak ... with regards to pricing,” but “none of our assumptions ... is built on those peak returns” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).
  • Nattel, RBC Capital Markets: asked if returns could exceed early assumptions; President Colizza responded, “yes, I do believe that there will be some of those sectors that will outperform and ingredients is likely one of them” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).
  • Derek Lessard, TD Cowen: asked about commitments and pricing into the second half; President Colizza said some contracts will lag at prior highs, some volumes are spot, and “we have seen some of the pricing come off of its ultimate highs,” while emphasizing “continued demand” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).
  • Lessard, TD Cowen: asked about industry cheese capacity; President Colizza referenced prior commentary on U.S. processing investment, noted cheese is growing slower than ingredients, and said “the 2 are fundamentally tied” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).
  • Christopher Li, Desjardins: asked about strong U.S. milk production and sustainability; President Colizza said the resilience is “surprising,” but “welcome,” citing feed costs, weather, genetics, and a “healthy beef market” as supports (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).
  • Li, Desjardins: asked about U.S. margin opportunities and timing of lapping ingredient tailwinds; President Colizza pointed to investments including Friendship and value-added beverages, and said pricing contracts are “typically ... 3, 4 months” and that WPC80 highs “will not necessarily be there in the more immediate future” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).
  • Vishal Shreedhar, National Bank Financial: asked about GLP-1 impacts and pizza softness; President Colizza said GLP-1s “are creating some new opportunities,” acknowledged pizza had “moments of softness,” and said mozzarella is finding outlets “domestic or from an export perspective” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).
  • Shreedhar, National Bank Financial: asked for quantitative EBITDA contribution from ingredients; President Colizza declined category disclosure but said “high-protein ingredients were the primary driver of our earnings growth this quarter” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).
  • John Zamparo, Scotiabank: asked what changed in Australia; President Colizza cited the post-optimization phase, milk allocation to “highest return categories,” and more milk availability supporting “fixed cost absorption” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).
  • Zamparo, Scotiabank: asked about buy vs. build and CapEx; President Colizza said Saputo will invest in cultured, beverages, and ingredients, while CFO Therrien highlighted flexibility below the 2.25x leverage target and said Saputo will remain “quite active” on the NCIB (CFO & Secretary Therrien).
  • Tamy Chen, BMO Capital Markets: asked about contracted vs. spot whey and product mix; President Colizza said “a large quantity” is contracted, emphasized balancing commitments with flexibility, and said Saputo can shift ingredient streams to “adapt to the market needs” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).
  • Scott Marks, Jefferies: asked about any demand weakness in ingredients and mix targets; President Colizza said ingredient demand is “still very strong,” and described “reformulations” shifting among dairy inputs rather than weakening demand (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).
  • Bahamin Abdolpanah, Ventum Financial: asked about Waupun utilization and sourcing; President Colizza said Waupun was built “with excess capacity,” and filling it includes “internalizing some solids” and “procuring liquid solids” regionally, adding, “that's exactly what Steve Douglas is focused on” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).
  • Tal Woolley, CIBC Capital Markets: asked about customer concentration, end uses, and tariff/supply management risk; President Colizza said ingredients are “very well diversified,” some products go to “infant nutrition,” and on trade said the impact “has not been material,” including the “ban with regards to whey solids from Canada entering the U.S.” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were slightly positive overall, frequently congratulating results while pressing on durability of ingredients pricing, mix concentration, Waupun utilization, and category offsets (e.g., demand sustainability, GLP-1 impacts, and cheese vs. ingredients sensitivity).
  • Management tone was positive and confident in prepared remarks and largely steady in Q&A, repeatedly characterizing protein demand as “structural,” while declining detailed profitability disclosures and emphasizing diversification and execution (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).
  • Versus last quarter, the discussion shifted from broad-based momentum and four-sector contributions to more concentrated analyst probing on ingredients pricing/contracting mechanics and utilization, with management adding clearer organizational actions (Ingredients Division creation; Canada leadership change) while maintaining a similar confidence level.

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • The reporting structure changed from four operating sectors (including Europe) last quarter to three sectors this quarter, as CFO Therrien said the Dairy Division (UK) is now treated as discontinued operations and “we now report 3 sectors: Canada, U.S. and international” (CFO & Secretary Therrien).
  • Portfolio actions escalated from last quarter’s Argentina stake sale and planned DSDA exit to this quarter’s expected $1.7 billion UK proceeds and continued expectation to close the DSDA transaction in Q3 fiscal 2027 (CFO & Secretary Therrien).
  • Management’s strategic emphasis stayed anchored on protein-aligned categories and operational productivity, but with sharper execution steps this quarter, including the Ingredients Division under Steve Douglas and expanded enterprise transformation leadership under Haig Poutchigian (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).
  • Analyst focus tightened quarter-over-quarter on the sustainability, contracting structure, and capacity-filling plan for high-protein ingredients, while also probing GLP-1 impacts and trade/tariff risk in Canada.

Risks and Concerns

  • Colizza cited ongoing inflation pressure: “Inflation remained a challenge across labor, fuel, transportation and packaging, and we are managing it through mitigation initiatives and pricing actions” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).
  • Management highlighted market volatility and trade uncertainty: “We recognize that volatility is the new normal. Market swings, trade uncertainty and cost pressures will continue” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).
  • On trade frictions, Colizza said the whey-solids ban from Canada to the U.S. “has created a wrinkle,” while adding Saputo is “still benefiting from adding value to those whey solids domestically in Canada” (President, Interim COO, CEO & Non-Independent Director Colizza).

Final Takeaway

Saputo’s Q2 fiscal 2027 narrative centered on high-protein ingredients as the primary earnings driver alongside operational efficiencies, while management moved to formalize ingredients as a standalone division under Steve Douglas and continued to simplify the footprint through the planned UK and DSDA exits. Management emphasized that demand for protein-aligned dairy is structural and broadening beyond ingredients into cultured and value-added products, while positioning capital allocation around organic investment, an active NCIB renewal plan, and balance-sheet flexibility supported by expected divestiture proceeds.

data.title: Brent crude caps biggest weekly drop since pandemic as war premium begins to unwind
data.description:
Crude oil futures finished little changed Friday but Brent crude ended with its largest weekly loss since the COVID-19 pandemic, after heavy losses suffered by Republicans in the U.S. midterm elections raised expectations that the Trump administration will pursue a diplomatic solution to the conflict with Iran.

This week saw "the reversal of the substantial risk premium that had accrued across September and October despite resilient Middle East flows and rapidly normalizing global oil balances," Macquarie energy strategist Walt Chancellor said in a note.

Previous worries over a potential escalation in the Middle East have "given way to a renewed diplomatic push, less hawkish rhetoric from Trump, and apparent Republican introspection about the war in the aftermath of the midterms," Chancellor wrote.

Bloomberg reported Friday that the U.S. and Iran have moved closer to a potential breakthrough in efforts to end the war, with Iran showing a willingness to discuss issues related to its nuclear program that were previously off the table.

Iran is studying proposals related to its atomic activities that were presented by chief mediator Qatar, and President Trump recently spoke by phone with Qatar's leader about efforts to de-escalate tensions, according to the report.

Physical oil prices are also signaling an easing in global supply conditions, and analysts at J.P. Morgan said this week that the global oil market is moving back into surplus as Middle Eastern exports recover and demand weakens.

Global supply exceeded demand by 1.1M bbl/day in September and widened to 1.4M bbl/day in October, while Middle Eastern oil exports recovered to 20.7M bbl/day in October from a low of 9.8M bbl/day in March during the first month of the war, the bank estimated.

Global oil demand has declined by 3.3M bbl/day since the conflict began, JPM also said, reflecting the impact of higher fuel prices and supply disruptions.

Nevertheless, the recovery in oil flows from the Middle East remains at risk due to attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and threats by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militants against Saudi Arabia and its Red Sea export route.

A Greek ship manager said a seafarer was killed in a November 5 explosion on an oil products tanker in the Persian Gulf, believed to have been caused by a missile attack.

Data from U.K. maritime security agency UKMTO suggested that attacks on oil-carrying ships are still running at close to a record pace.

On Friday, front-month Nymex crude (CL1:COM) for December delivery edged up 0.3% to $90.83/bbl and front-month Brent crude (CO1:COM) for December delivery gained $0.03 to $98.32/bbl.

For the full week, U.S. crude plunged 12.7%, its biggest one week percentage decline since the week ending April 17, and Brent crude sank 13.3%, its largest one week percentage loss since the week ending April 24, 2020.

U.S. natural gas futures (NG1:COM) gained as some cooler weather entered into the latest weather forecasts, lifting the front-month Nymex contract for December delivery up 1.7% to $2.998/MMBtu, its best settlement value since October 19; for the week, U.S. natgas gained 3.4%.

Energy stocks, as represented by the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE), tumbled 12% this week.

data.title: Treace outlines $206M-$210M 2026 revenue range while targeting $700M TAM expansion
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Treace Medical Concepts (TMCI) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "We're encouraged by our third quarter performance, driven by double-digit case volume growth and continued market share gains" (Founder, Chairman & CEO John Treace).

  • "We're narrowing our full year 2026 revenue guidance to be in the range of $206 million to $210 million" and "this outlook assumes a return to growth in the fourth quarter" (CEO Treace).

  • "We expect the new 2026 product introductions that I will discuss this morning to expand our total addressable market by approximately $700 million" (CEO Treace).

  • "Through the third quarter, approximately 45% of our Lapiplasty surgeons used at least 1 of these 3 new bunion systems in their practice, up from 40% in Q2" and "we also continue to see approximately 30% of surgeons who initially became Treace customers through these new bunion systems now using Lapiplasty products" (CEO Treace).

  • "We are in final preparations for the anticipated commercial launch of our Lightning system in Q1 2027" and "we anticipate full commercialization of this new [Tailorplasty] system within Q1 of 2027" (CEO Treace).

  • "Revenue in the third quarter was $48.3 million, a decrease of 4% compared to the prior-year period" and "gross margin was 79.5%" (Chief Financial Officer Mark Hair).

  • "Third quarter net loss decreased... to $12.6 million, or $0.19 per share" and "Adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter was a positive $0.3 million" (CFO Hair).

Outlook

  • "We are narrowing our full year guidance and expect full year 2026 revenue to be in the range of $206 million to $210 million" and "we are updating our expectation of a loss in Adjusted EBITDA to be in the range of $1 million to $2 million for the full year 2026" (CFO Hair).

  • "This compares to the previous revenue guidance of $204 million to $212 million" (CEO Treace).

  • "This outlook assumes a return to growth in the fourth quarter" and is tied to "continued procedure volume increases" plus lapping "the ASP mix shift dynamics related to our 2025 product launches" and benefiting from "our 2026 product launches" (CEO Treace).

Financial Results

  • "The decline was mainly driven by the shift in revenue mix towards lower-priced, minimally invasive products and a lower volume of bunion procedure kits sold" (CFO Hair).

  • "Excluding sales to stocking distributors, bunion kit sales volume increased and revenue grew mid-single digits" and "we anticipate the revenue impact from stocking distributor orders will significantly decrease after the third quarter" (CFO Hair).

  • "Total operating expenses decreased $5.5 million or 10% to $49.9 million" and "Year-to-date cash usage was reduced by 53%, or $9.7 million" (CFO Hair).

  • "Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $39.8 million as of September 30, 2026" (CFO Hair).

Q&A

  • Ryan Zimmerman, BTIG: asked how ASP evolves as TMCI broadens wallet share; Founder, Chairman & CEO Treace: "we're seeing the gap trend in the right direction here, this ASP mix gap" and "overall ASPs or revenue per case may come down a bit" while also citing "some very high ASP cases" in midfoot/rearfoot.

  • Ryan Zimmerman, BTIG: asked about execution risk entering Q4 with many launches; CEO Treace: "Our strategy here is to build a large, diversified foot and ankle business off of our anchor as the leader in the bunion space" and "we've hired a lot of reps that have competitive company foot and ankle experience."

  • Benjamin Haynor, Lake Street: asked whether adoption can keep rising from 45%; CEO Treace: "we're not done" and "we'd love to have 100% of these surgeons using 1 or more" while also pushing deeper multi-product usage.

  • Benjamin Haynor, Lake Street: asked about international expansion timing; CEO Treace: "international is something we understand is a real opportunity" but "if and when we get to a point where there's something material, we'll let you know."

  • Frederick Wise, Stifel: asked why the high end of revenue guidance narrowed despite Q3 upside and about consumer/elective demand; CFO Hair: "Our views on Q4 are really unchanged" and emphasized the Q3 stocking-distributor comp; CEO Treace: "we were in a little different situation" because portfolio expansion and SuperBite brought "new incremental procedures."

  • Frederick Wise, Stifel: asked about reorder behavior after first trial; CEO Treace: "The reorder rate... is... pretty high" and cited growth in "the 2-plus category and the 3-plus category."

  • Frederick Wise, Stifel: pressed on 2027 growth framing; CFO Hair: "before we really dive deep into 2027... we plan to give our guidance on our Q4 call" and "we really want to better understand these case volumes in our seasonally strongest quarter."

  • Kunal (for Richard Newitter), Truist: asked about rep headcount needs and OpEx direction as portfolio expands; CEO Treace: "we will continue to modestly build our sales channel" with adds that are "more incremental"; CFO Hair: "we're not anticipating dramatic changes to our OpEx" and highlighted that sales adds are "variable costs" under commissions.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Slightly negative to neutral analyst tone, with repeated probing on pricing/ASP pressure, guidance conservatism, and execution risk into Q4; for example, Stifel questioned why TMCI "brought the upper end down" (Frederick Wise, Stifel).

  • Slightly positive management tone in both prepared remarks and Q&A, leaning on validation from volumes and launches; CEO Treace said "we're seeing the gap trend in the right direction" and CFO Hair said "We remain confident in the seasonally strong Q4."

  • Versus Q2, management language shifted from "raising our full year 2026 revenue guidance" (Q2) to "narrowing" the range (Q3), while maintaining the Q4 "return to positive revenue growth" message across both calls.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Guidance posture changed from Q2 "we are raising our full year 2026 revenue guidance to be in the range of $204 million to $212 million" to Q3 "narrowing... to... $206 million to $210 million" (CEO Treace).

  • Product cadence expanded from Q2 limited SuperBite release and discussion of CartiBlaster to Q3 describing four 2026 additions (SuperBite, HyperPlate, VitaFuse, CartiBlaster) and initial Tailorplasty cases, alongside Lightning and IntelliGuide updates (CEO Treace).

  • Pricing/ASP discussion remained a central theme, but Q3 emphasized the portfolio-driven mix outlook: "overall ASPs or revenue per case may come down a bit" while citing offsetting "very high ASP cases" (CEO Treace).

Risks and Concerns

  • Mix and kit dynamics remained a headwind: "shift in revenue mix towards lower-priced, minimally invasive products" and "lower volume of bunion procedure kits sold" (CFO Hair).

  • Visibility and execution risk into the peak season were acknowledged through conservatism: "The magnitude of the Q3 beat... is relatively modest" and TMCI kept Q4 expectations "very achievable" (CFO Hair).

  • Commercial complexity increased with a larger bag: "there are a lot of new technologies coming into the reps' hands" and TMCI is "spending a lot of time training them" (CEO Treace).

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q3 around procedure growth and share gains while acknowledging ongoing ASP/mix pressure from lower-priced minimally invasive products. The company tightened full-year revenue guidance to $206 million-$210 million and updated expected full-year Adjusted EBITDA loss to $1 million-$2 million, while reiterating a Q4 return to growth supported by easier stocking-distributor comparisons and 2026 product launches. Leadership highlighted adoption momentum across newer bunion systems, upcoming Q1 2027 Lightning and Tailorplasty commercialization, and a stated approximately $700 million expansion of total addressable market tied to the 2026 launch cadence and broader foot-and-ankle push.

data.title: Gogo reiterates $870M-$895M 2026 revenue guidance while outlining Galileo speeds to over 1 gigabit by 2032
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Gogo (GOGO) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "In the third quarter, we continued to execute on our transformation from a domestic Air-to-Ground connectivity company into a global provider of high-speed broadband to the underpenetrated business and military government aviation markets." (CEO & Director Christopher Moore)

  • "We are pleased with the strong progress and growing momentum across our next-generation broadband technology portfolio, including record shipments of Gogo Galileo in the quarter." (CEO & Director Moore) "We unveiled a multiyear technology road map that gives customers clear visibility into the future of their Gogo Galileo investment, taking speeds to over 1 gigabit by 2032." (CEO & Director Moore)

  • "We are very appreciative of our advisers and lenders who believe in the transformation of our business and agreed to amend and extend our approximately $600 million of Original Term Loan B debt." (CEO & Director Moore) "We are working with our banking advisers and other industry and regulatory specialists to evaluate the full range of possibilities for capitalizing on our spectrum and tower assets, determine their highest and best use and realize the value for shareholders and customers." (CEO & Director Moore)

  • "We had a record quarter of shipments for Galileo of 172 units, a 59% increase from the second quarter and a 95% increase year-over-year." (CEO & Director Moore) "We also ended the quarter with 297 Galileo aircraft online, up 61% from the prior quarter." (CEO & Director Moore)

  • "This quarter, we secured the renewal of a sovereign communications lease valued at more than $15 million annually to provide GEO connectivity to an overseas government customer." (CEO & Director Moore)

  • "Gogo's total revenue for the quarter was $213.2 million, down 5% compared to Q3 2025 and 4% compared to Q2 2026." (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Zachary Cotner) "Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was $41 million." (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner)

Outlook

  • "We are reiterating our full year guidance." (CEO & Director Moore) "We continue to expect total revenue in the range of $870 million to $895 million... We expect adjusted EBITDA in the range of $175 million to $185 million." (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner)

  • "That range now includes approximately $18 million of ongoing litigation expense, down from $22 million in our prior guidance following the Delaware District Court's ruling in the SmartSky matter." (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner)

  • "Net capital expenditures are still planned to be approximately $20 million." (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner) "This now assumes $35 million in FCC reimbursement, down from $45 million, reflecting longer processing time for program modifications... shifting into 2027." (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner)

Financial Results

  • "Service revenue totaled $182.7 million." (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner) "Equipment revenue totaled $30.5 million." (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner)

  • "Gross margin for the quarter before depreciation and amortization was approximately 40% compared to 42% in the second quarter, driven by lower ATG service revenue, which carries our highest margins." (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner)

  • "The net loss for the quarter was $3.2 million." (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner) "Third quarter results include a $6.1 million noncash increase in the fair value of the Satcom Direct earn-out liability." (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner)

  • "Free cash flow was $28.1 million." (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner) "We ended the quarter with $90.7 million in cash and cash equivalents." (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner)

Q&A

  • Justin Lang, Morgan Stanley, Research Division: "So just curious, if you could talk a little bit more about what's on the table in terms of highest and best use"; CEO & Director Moore: "We believe that even with our network utilization across our ATG customers, there is still room for further extraction of value." "The amazing thing with our spectrum... is that it actually can be applied across those 3 areas" (unmanned aircraft systems, terrestrial mobile carriers, and D2D).

  • Justin Lang, Morgan Stanley, Research Division: "updated expectations around the shape of growth in Galileo AOL into next year and then maybe early HDX, FDX breakdown?"; Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner: "it's still predominantly HDX" and "we aren't giving 2027 guidance on this call" while adding "we feel confident that the demand is still strong."

  • Scott Searle, ROTH Capital Partners, LLC, Research Division: "what still is at risk" in ATG transitions and "how much of that is churning off"; Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner: "we still anticipate the net Air-to-Ground tail to be down about 1,200" and later added "within those deactivation numbers, 71 are upgrades either to Galileo or 5G that's not been activated, with obviously the vast majority being Galileo."

  • Scott Searle, ROTH Capital Partners, LLC, Research Division: "Is there a time line that you're comfortable with that the ATG business will bottom?"; CEO & Director Moore: "I think it's a bit too early to give you the exact timing of that" and "we're now planning on doing the flash cut into Q1 next year."

  • Scott Searle, ROTH Capital Partners, LLC, Research Division: "Is there a growth rate that you're comfortable with for the Mil/Gov business"; CEO & Director Moore: "I think we don't want to discuss the growth percentages on the call" and "we're very... optimistic about this segment."

  • Scott Searle, ROTH Capital Partners, LLC, Research Division: litigation and 2027 OpEx; Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner: "It should come down dramatically." "Our current estimate is about half of what we spent this year." and "OpEx, excluding G&A, should kind of hang out around the high 100s, low 200s."

Sentiment Analysis

  • "Just curious" and "how developed some of that thinking is?" (Justin Lang, Morgan Stanley, Research Division), plus repeated spectrum follow-up questions, signaled a slightly negative-to-neutral analyst tone focused on monetization timing and certainty.

  • "it's a bit too early" (CEO & Director Moore) and "we aren't giving 2027 guidance" (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner) indicated a neutral management tone in Q&A, while prepared remarks leaned slightly positive with "record quarter of shipments" and "we are reiterating our full year guidance." (CEO & Director Moore)

  • Compared with Q2, management repeated a similar framing of transformation ("we continue to execute on our transformation" (CEO & Director Moore) in both quarters), while Q3 featured more emphasis on balance-sheet actions and asset optionality.

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Q3 introduced a spectrum and tower asset value workstream following the renewal: "the FCC recently granted us a 10-year license renewal" and "we are working with our banking advisers" on "capitalizing on our spectrum and tower assets" (CEO & Director Moore); Q2 described the UAV work as earlier stage: "While this work remains at an early stage" (CEO & Director Moore).

  • Q3 detailed a longer-term Galileo performance plan: "planned performance enhancements approximately every 24 months" and "targeting download speeds of 5x and upload speeds of 10x current levels" (CEO & Director Moore), while Q2 emphasized near-term ramp mechanics such as STC timing and OEM process: "we've still got 20 STCs outstanding with the FDX" and "that process... also takes time" (CEO & Director Moore).

  • Q3 maintained guidance but revised litigation and FCC reimbursement assumptions: "approximately $18 million of ongoing litigation expense" and "assumes $35 million in FCC reimbursement" (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner); Q2 guidance included "approximately $22 million of ongoing litigation expense" and "assuming $45 million in FCC reimbursement" (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner).

Risks and Concerns

  • "Total ATG aircraft online ended the quarter at 5,399, down 6% sequentially" and "ATG service revenue decreased due to customer deactivations" (CEO & Director Moore), with management pointing to mitigation via migration: "ATG customers upgrade directly to Galileo" (CEO & Director Moore).

  • "Galileo equipment carries lower margins than the ATG hardware it is replacing" (CEO & Director Moore) and "several fleet orders were aggressively priced" (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner), with management tying strategy to duration: "each aircraft that activates represents a 7- to 10-year recurring revenue relationship." (CEO & Director Moore)

  • "Final judgment has not yet been entered and the litigation remains ongoing." (CEO & Director Moore)

Final Takeaway

Management emphasized that Q3 results reflected a planned transition away from legacy ATG, highlighted "record" Galileo shipments and a multiyear road map "taking speeds to over 1 gigabit by 2032" (CEO & Director Moore), reiterated full-year guidance while lowering expected 2026 litigation expense and FCC reimbursement assumptions (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Cotner), and described new financial and strategic optionality via a Term Loan B amendment/extension and an active review of how to "extract the most amount of value" from spectrum and tower assets. (CEO & Director Moore)

data.title: Starwood signals board review of dividend policy while targeting $800m-plus of 2026 legacy asset resolutions
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Starwood Property Trust (STWD) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "DE was $0.31 per share in the quarter or $0.41, excluding realized gains and losses from commercial lending resolution" (CFO, Treasurer, Principal Financial Officer & Chief Accounting Officer Rina Paniry). Paniry added that the company "added this new measure of distributable earnings" in its press release supplement and 10-Q.
  • "During the quarter, we resolved $254 million of nonaccrual and REO" (CFO Paniry), including "the sale of 2 multifamily REO assets" and sales of "2 units in our New York City residential project." She also said the company returned "the final $108 million portion" of a Brooklyn office loan to accrual after achieving "100% occupancy."
  • "We originated $2.4 billion of investments in the quarter, of which $1.5 billion was funded" (CFO Paniry), and the commercial lending portfolio rose "to a record $17.8 billion." She reported reserves of "$1 billion" against nonaccrual and REO, and said undepreciated book value was "$17.22" per share.
  • "We completed over $250 million of resolutions in the quarter and remain on track to achieve the over $800 million resolution target for 2026" (President & Director Jeffrey Dimodica). He added: "We had no new nonaccrual loans and no new foreclosures again this quarter."
  • "In the quarter, we repurchased $108 million of common stock, bringing year-to-date repurchases to $138 million" (President Dimodica), while highlighting early repayment of "$500 million of corporate debt" and the company’s focus on lowering funding costs.
  • "Given all these uncertainties, I think we will have to examine what we're going to do with our dividend" (CEO & Non-Independent Executive Chairman Barry Sternlicht). Sternlicht said the dividend "has been paid well above the DE rates" recently and added, "We will have a meeting with our Board and discuss this."

Outlook

  • Dividend policy became a new explicit near-term decision point versus the prior quarter: "we will have to examine what we're going to do with our dividend" (CEO Sternlicht), alongside his view that the company should "reduce the dividend and then have increase it as we get the earnings power" back.
  • The legacy-asset clean-up target was reiterated: "remain on track to achieve the over $800 million resolution target for 2026" (President Dimodica), and Sternlicht later said, "We expect to hit the $850-ish million that we told you about for the year."
  • On forward earnings framing, management positioned the new metric as a baseline: "I think you can use that as sort of a base earnings rate" (CEO Sternlicht), referring to the $0.41 DE excluding realized items discussed in Q&A.
  • No revenue or GAAP EPS guidance was provided in the prepared remarks or Q&A included in this transcript.

Financial Results

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: slightly negative to pressing, centered on reserve sustainability, credit migration, and dividend risk, including direct probing like "kitchen sink" framing (Donald Fandetti, Wells Fargo) and repeated checks on incremental defaults (Jade Rahmani, KBW).
  • Management: slightly negative on near-term uncertainty but confident on strategy execution; CEO Sternlicht used cautionary framing such as "we can't tell you" on reserve path and "we will have to examine" the dividend, while also asserting, "Starwood is uniquely positioned really to handle all this stuff" and emphasizing diversification.
  • Versus last quarter, management’s tone shifted from "we're not considering our dividend -- changing our dividend policy at the moment" (CEO Sternlicht, Q2) to an explicit board-level review in Q3, while analysts remained focused on rates, multifamily risk, and business-model valuation.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Dividend stance changed most visibly: in Q2, CEO Sternlicht said, "we're not considering our dividend -- changing our dividend policy at the moment"; in Q3, he said, "we will have to examine what we're going to do with our dividend" and planned a board discussion.
  • Reserve and book value narrative intensified: Q3 featured a large reserve build attributed to the third-party model and rates, plus a book value impact from swaps; Q2 discussed smaller model-driven reserve change and upcoming Q3 realized loss expectations tied to asset sales.
  • Capital allocation messaging evolved from Q2’s emphasis on debt issuance and balance sheet extension to Q3’s emphasis on buybacks ("$108 million" in-quarter) and continued legacy resolutions ("over $800 million" 2026 target reiterated).
  • Strategic optionality around net lease became more explicit in Q3: CEO Sternlicht said the platform "either should raise outside capital or spin out from us," building on Q2 commentary that a net lease separation was an option "in our pocket."

Risks and Concerns

  • Interest-rate sensitivity and model-driven reserves were the core risk highlighted: "The bulk of this quarter's reserve increase was driven by that increase in interest rates" (President Dimodica), and CEO Sternlicht said the forward curve is embedded in CECL.
  • Multifamily refinance risk was repeatedly linked to rates and cap rates: President Dimodica described downgrades concentrated in pre-2023 originations and CEO Sternlicht said, "many borrowers are definitely hurting" with the curve "shifted higher."
  • Dividend sustainability risk was directly raised by management: CEO Sternlicht said the dividend has been "paid well above the DE rates" and the company would discuss prudence with its board.
  • Net lease growth constraints were tied to cost of capital and market activity: CEO Sternlicht said, "Our cost of capital is a little high," and President Dimodica said, "Sale leaseback volume has fallen off a cliff."

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q3 around a higher-rate shock flowing through CECL and book value, ongoing resolutions and repayments in legacy assets, and diversification benefits across servicing, infrastructure, and property. The most material new signal versus last quarter was CEO Sternlicht’s statement that the board will “examine” dividend policy given recent DE levels, alongside continued capital actions including sizable buybacks and a reiterated 2026 resolution target above $800 million.
